name: Bodyless — Anti-Physicality Youth Movement
description: Bodyless emerged among Tier 2-3 youth as a philosophical and aesthetic rejection of the body as primary identity — not aug-rejection and not aug-positivity, but a position that the physical form is increasingly irrelevant in a world of BCI immersion, digital-physical blending, and identity construction through data. Members spend maximized time in deep BCI states and minimize attention to physical presentation: they wear identical, neutral gray garments called 'shells' and consider elaborate body modification or fashion as 'loud flesh' — a term of mild contempt. Paradoxically, their BCI-space avatars are extraordinarily elaborate and expressive. Identity is constructed entirely in digital space.
cultural_impact: Bodyless has created serious concern among neurologists about extended BCI immersion patterns in adolescents, and three corponations have quietly funded studies framing the movement as a public health crisis. The movement has influenced a generation of BCI-space architecture and avatar design.
key_figures: Nneka Johansson-Patel (founder, known only by avatar name 'Voidform')
locations: The Shell (physical meeting space, deliberately featureless, Tier 3 North)
Bodyless Pods (shared immersion housing, Milwaukee Corridor)
story_hooks: A Bodyless member's physical body is found in medical distress while their mind is deep in BCI space — their community doesn't have protocols for physical emergency and their family has no idea where they are.
A Tier 5 corporation wants to hire Bodyless members as BCI-space architects, offering extraordinary compensation — the movement fractures over whether accepting corporate work betrays the philosophy.
A Bodyless youth disappears from both physical and digital space simultaneously — their 'shell' is found empty, their avatar vanished, and no one knows if this was intentional.
